runs.question: Which AI regulatory instrument best reduces expected harm from frontier AI over the next five years, keeping the technology sector's net loss below $400bn and the gross social cost under $150bn?

Compare strict liability with liability under a safe harbour and mandatory third party evaluations over the next five years; the technology sector's net loss must stay below $300bn and the probability of a catastrophic incident must fall by at least a quarter.
Would a six month moratorium above the compute threshold or coordinated frontier licensing reduce expected harm more over three years, keeping the gross social cost under $100bn?

shared.run_idle: A policy question is read into a battery of candidate instruments. Gate 1 runs the battery and Gate 2 releases the briefing; either can be refused with a reason. This public demonstration takes no sign off identities; inside an authority a named preparer and a named approver on the register take the gates, with four eyes. Every step is chained into a signed ledger.
